== Biography ==
John Glasgow is estimated to have been born around 1785, likely in County Tyrone, Ireland. This estimation is based on the approximate birth year of his eldest known son, Henry (c. 1810).

John Glasgow's existence and paternity are established through the records of his sons, Henry and Benjamin. The marriage record for Benjamin Glasgow identifies his father as John Glasgow.<ref name="BenjaminMarriage">Inferred from the marriage record of son [[Glasgow-2059|Benjamin Glasgow]], which names his father as John. (Specific citation for the marriage record should be added here when available).</ref> The familial link between Benjamin and Henry is confirmed by Henry's will, which names Benjamin as his brother.<ref name="HenryWill">Inferred from the will of [[Glasgow-1735|Henry Glasgow]], which identifies [[Glasgow-2059|Benjamin Glasgow]] as his brother. (Specific citation for the will abstract should be added here when available).</ref>

Henry’s brother Benjamin’s original 1856 marriage calls their father John Glasgow, '''merchant'''

It is tentatively assumed that John resided in or near Killycurragh townland, Derryloran Parish, County Tyrone, as this location is associated with his sons.

Known children:
* [[Glasgow-1735|Henry Glasgow]] (abt. 1810-1874)<ref name="HenryWill"/>
* [[Glasgow-2059|Benjamin Glasgow]] (abt. 1835-1870)<ref name="BenjaminMarriage"/>

== Research Notes ==
'''Evidence Trail:'''
The profile for this John Glasgow is constructed based on the following derivative evidence:
# [[Glasgow-1735|Henry Glasgow]] (d. 1874) left a will mentioning his brother, [[Glasgow-2059|Benjamin Glasgow]].
# The marriage record for Benjamin Glasgow names his father as John Glasgow.
# Therefore, John Glasgow is inferred to be the father of both Henry and Benjamin.

'''Location:''' The location of Killycurragh Townland, Derryloran Parish, is assumed based on the known residency of his sons.

'''Potential Match:''' It is possible that this profile represents the same person as [[Glasgow-1968|John Glasgow (abt.1775-)]], who also resided in the area. Further research is needed to confirm or deny this connection.

'''Birth Date Gap:''' There is a significant gap (approx. 25 years) between the estimated birth dates of Henry (c. 1810) and Benjamin (c. 1835). This may suggest two different mothers, or that the estimated dates require refinement.

=== Merchant named in Benjamin’s marriage ===

The original marriage entry for [[Glasgow-2059|Benjamin Glasgow]] and [[Little-17969|Jane Little]], dated 15 April 1856 at First Presbyterian Church, Cookstown, names John Glasgow as Benjamin’s father and describes him as a merchant. Benjamin was a bachelor merchant, aged 20, resident in Cookstown; Jane was a full-age spinster of Oritor Craigs, daughter of George Little, farmer. The witnesses were John Potter and George Potter.<ref>[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1856/09507/5445820.pdf Cookstown civil marriage return, 15 April 1856, printed p.273, entry 43].</ref> The entry does not state John’s age, residence or parents.

The full viewer reading of the 22 July 1858 mill case supersedes the prior ambiguous assessment: Benjamin Glasgow testified that he was the son of the late Robert Glasgow, had managed his father’s mill since 1850, and that Robert died in 1856. Counsel referred to Robert’s sons, supporting a qualified brother inference for co-plaintiff William Glasgow. Benjamin’s evidence says “witness’s uncle, Mr. Glasgow, sen.”; the William identification is attributed separately to case context; the report does not state whether that was paternal or maternal. Mothers remain unknown. This evidence concerns Benjamin’s family and does not establish parents for John Glasgow.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390574459/ Belfast News-Letter, 22 July 1858, p.3].</ref>

A possible identification concerns John Glasgow, Cookstown merchant and tea/coffee agent, 1848–1850. John Glasgow, explicitly called a merchant at Cookstown, appears among John Cassell coffee agents on 30 September 1848, and again in February 1849. A separate 2 February 1849 advertisement appoints him there as agent for the Russian Company’s Caravan Tea and Arabian Coffee. The Russian Company agent list is repeated on 13 April 1849, again explicitly calling John a merchant at Cookstown. Two further inspected 1849 notices give the same merchant wording, each from a distinct issue.<ref>The Sligo Champion, 30 September 1848, p.3, John Cassell coffee agents; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1256974148/ record]; Belfast News-Letter, 2 February 1849, p.3, Russian Company tea and coffee agents; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390559166/ record]; Belfast News-Letter, 20 February 1849, p.3, John Cassell coffee agents; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390559823/ record]; Impartial Reporter and Farmers’ Journal, 22 February 1849, p.3, John Cassell coffee agents; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1257358494/ record]; Belfast News-Letter, 1849-04-13, p.3; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390562652/ record]; Impartial Reporter and Farmers’ Journal, 31 May 1849, p.3, John Cassell agents; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1257358629/ record]; The Sligo Champion, 3 November 1849, p. 1, John Cassell coffee agents; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1256975442/ record]; The Sligo Champion, 28 July 1849, p. 3, John Cassell coffee agents; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1256975114/ record].</ref> [[Glasgow-2058]] is compatible by name, Cookstown district and the merchant occupation independently recorded in [[Glasgow-2059]]’s 1856 marriage. None of these advertisements names relatives, age or street address. Repeated agent lists are advertisements for one trading role, not independent family proofs. John’s parents remain unknown. [[Glasgow-1968]] remains a weaker comparison: his family histories give migration to Michigan in 1844 or 1848; the Drummeen tithe and 1850/1851 probate leads are not securely assigned to him, and probate year is not a death date. The 5 September 1850 notice lists John as an appointed Cookstown agent but does not call him a merchant, name relatives or state a residence. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns John Glasgow, Cookstown merchant and tea/coffee agent, 1848–1850. John Glasgow is listed at Cookstown among retail agents for John Cassell’s coffees in November 1850.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 5 November 1850, p.3, John Cassell coffee agents, Cookstown; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390563426/ record].</ref> [[Glasgow-2058|John Glasgow]], later described as a merchant in his son’s 1856 marriage, is compatible by name, trade and district. The advertisement gives no age, exact address or relatives, so it does not prove that identification or identify Benjamin’s grandparents. Other local Johns remain comparisons; no parent or brother is attached from this advertisement. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns John Glasgow, Cookstown merchant and tea/coffee agent, 1848–1850. John Cassell coffee and five-shilling tea advertisement: Cookstown—John Glasgow, among the appointed agents. Coffee-only advertisements on 17 August and 4 October 1850 also list John Glasgow at Cookstown; neither calls him a merchant. The 5 September 1850 appointed-agent notice names Cookstown—John Glasgow, without the merchant title.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 22 February 1850, p.3, Cassell tea and coffee agents; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390556388/ record]; Belfast News-Letter, 8 March 1850, p.3, John Cassell coffee and tea agents; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390556799/ record]; The Sligo Champion, 1850-08-17, p.3, John Cassell coffee agents; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1256976506/ record]; Belfast News-Letter, 1850-10-04, p.3, John Cassell coffee agents; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390562655/ record]; The Fermanagh Mail, and Enniskillen Chronicle, 5 September 1850, p. 3, John Cassell appointed agents; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1369100894/ record].</ref> A further original advertisement in the 1848–1850 Cookstown trading sequence, including Cassell tea as well as coffee. [[Glasgow-2058|John Glasgow]] remains compatible by name, locality and merchant occupation; no age, address, parents or uncle link appears. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns John Glasgow, Dundrum subscription-list context, 1840. John Glasgow occurs in the Loyal National Repeal Association subscription report, under “Per Mr. Edward Byrne, Dundrum,” published on 19 October 1840. This is a personal surname occurrence in a named collection list.<ref>Freeman’s Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 19 October 1840, p.4, Loyal National Repeal Association subscriptions; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050137248/ record]; Freeman’s Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 19 October 1840, p. 4, Loyal National Repeal Association subscriptions (alternate scan); [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1380778107/ record].</ref> The list supplies no age, occupation, exact address, relatives or individual subscription amount. Dundrum identifies the collection context; it is not an explicit statement of John’s residence. [[Glasgow-2058]], [[Glasgow-1968]] and [[Glasgow-2056]] survive as chronology comparisons only; none has a checked Dublin or Dundrum bridge. No identification or religious affiliation is inferred from the political subscription. Image 1380778107 is an alternate scan of this same report and list passage, not a second occurrence. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns John Glasgow, Loughinsholin freeholder, 1831. The 16 August 1831 declaration lists Robert Glasgow and John Glasgow among freeholders of the barony printed Loughinshollen (modern Loughinsholin), County Londonderry, supporting Sir Robert Bateson. They are co-signatories; no kinship, occupation, age or individual townland is given. Castledawson and 4 July 1831 refer to the opposing meeting discussed in the declaration, not their homes or their signing date.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 16 August 1831, p.3, Loughinshollen freeholders’ declaration; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390548642/ record].</ref> [[Glasgow-2058]], [[Glasgow-3927]] (an indexed freeholder with uncertain locality), [[Glasgow-2990]] and [[Glasgow-4090]] remain adult regional comparisons. No same-name co-signature establishes descent, brotherhood or identity with the Cookstown merchant. The declaration concerns a holding in the barony, not necessarily residence there. The identification remains uncertain.

=== Military surgeons J. and John Glasco, 1816–1839 ===

An appointment dated 8 February 1816 names Assistant Surgeon J. Glasco of the 59th Foot as surgeon. An October 1822 notice places Surgeon John Glasco, from half-pay of the 59th, in the 60th Foot. A June 1825 Hospital Staff notice names Staff-Surgeon John Glasco for brevet deputy inspector; in 1826 a replacement succeeded the promoted 60th Foot surgeon Glasco, and a separate August notice names John Glasco, senior, retiring upon half-pay. In December 1836 Staff-Surgeon John Glasco, recently employed at Grenada, was appointed surgeon of the Liverpool Recruiting District. A Liverpool subscription in 1838 names Staff-Surgeon Glasco, and a September 1839 notice names John Glasco retiring upon half-pay. The senior retiree and later staff surgeon may be different men.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050078150/ Freeman's Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 1816-02-28, p.3].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050080149/ Freeman's Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 1822-10-02, p.4].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050086323/ Freeman's Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 1825-06-21, p.3].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050127796/ Freeman's Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 1826-05-16, p.3].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050043397/ Freeman's Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 1826-08-18, p.1].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050083649/ Freeman's Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 1836-12-30, p.1].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050130719/ Freeman's Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 1838-08-31, p.2].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1259428783/ The Drogheda Argus and Leinster Journal, 1839-09-28, p.4].</ref>

The later Cookstown merchant’s birth estimate fits the service period but supplies no military bridge. The 59th Foot descriptions support probable continuity between 1816 and 1822; senior in 1826 remains material, and the later Liverpool surgeon may be a second man. [[Glasgow-3927|John Glasco of Inishrush]] is another weak comparison. [[Glasgow-822|John Glasgow]] has Ohio evidence from 1833 that conflicts with the later Liverpool sequence. No service record proves these candidates to be the surgeons.

=== John Glasgow, Cookstown tea and coffee agent, 1848–1850 ===

John Glasgow, expressly styled merchant at Cookstown, appears in John Cassell coffee-agent advertisements from September 1848 and in the Russian Company’s Caravan Tea and Arabian Coffee agency list in February and April 1849. Further Cassell advertisements in 1849 and 1850 name John or Jno. Glasgow at Cookstown for coffee and tea. The repeated lists give no age, relatives or street address.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1256974148/ The Sligo Champion, 30 September 1848, p.3, John Cassell coffee agents].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390559166/ Belfast News-Letter, 2 February 1849, p.3, Russian Company tea and coffee agents].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390559823/ Belfast News-Letter, 20 February 1849, p.3, John Cassell coffee agents].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1257358494/ Impartial Reporter and Farmers’ Journal, 22 February 1849, p.3, John Cassell coffee agents].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390562652/ Belfast News-Letter, 1849-04-13, p.3].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1257358629/ Impartial Reporter and Farmers’ Journal, 31 May 1849, p.3, John Cassell agents].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1256975442/ The Sligo Champion, 3 November 1849, p. 1, John Cassell coffee agents].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1256975114/ The Sligo Champion, 28 July 1849, p. 3, John Cassell coffee agents].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390563426/ Belfast News-Letter, 5 November 1850, p.3, John Cassell coffee agents, Cookstown].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390556388/ Belfast News-Letter, 22 February 1850, p.3, Cassell tea and coffee agents].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390556799/ Belfast News-Letter, 8 March 1850, p.3, John Cassell coffee and tea agents].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1256976506/ The Sligo Champion, 1850-08-17, p.3, John Cassell coffee agents].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390562655/ Belfast News-Letter, 1850-10-04, p.3, John Cassell coffee agents].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1369100894/ The Fermanagh Mail, and Enniskillen Chronicle, 5 September 1850, p. 3, John Cassell appointed agents].</ref>

The agency notices fit John’s name, Cookstown district and merchant occupation independently given in Benjamin’s 1856 marriage. They do not name Benjamin or Henry, so the household identification remains compatible rather than proved. [[Glasgow-1968|John Glasgow]] is a weaker comparison because the reported move to Michigan in 1844 or 1848 conflicts with a continuing Irish agency; probate year alone does not establish his death.
